model.description: One row per quarter carrying the published INSEE ILO labour-market indicators for France including Mayotte, seasonally adjusted. Every value is published by INSEE; nothing here is computed from anything else.
model.name: french_labour_market_quarterly

questions.derivation: Select the published ILO unemployment rate and the published count of unemployed people by quarter. Neither is derived from the other.
questions.question: How many people in France are unemployed on the ILO definition, and what share of the labour force is that?

questions.derivation: Select the three published age-band unemployment rates and their matching counts by quarter. The bands partition the labour force, so the counts sum to the total.
questions.question: How far apart are the unemployment rates of under-25s, 25-to-49-year-olds and people aged 50 or over?

questions.derivation: Select each published slack measure with both its count and its own published rate. The rates are NOT comparable with one another: unemployment and long-term unemployment are shares of the labour force, the halo is a share of the population, and underemployment is a share of employment.
questions.question: Beyond headline ILO unemployment, how large are long-term unemployment, the halo around unemployment and underemployment?

questions.derivation: Select the published activity rate for both sexes together and for each sex, on both the all-ages and the 15-to-64 basis. The ALL-AGES basis is the one that matches the OECD's 15-or-over participation rate; the 15-to-64 basis is a narrower population and must never be placed on the same axis as an OECD figure.
questions.question: What share of the population takes part in the labour market, and how far apart are men and women?

questions.derivation: Select the published unemployment rate and count for each sex by quarter.
questions.question: Are men and women unemployed at different rates?

temporal.meaning: Each period is the first day of the calendar quarter the observation describes, from the provider's YYYY-Qn period. Only quarters carrying every declared indicator are published, which begins at 2003-Q1: the unemployment counts reach back to 1975 but the rates, halo, underemployment and activity series do not.

validations.description: There is exactly one row for each quarter.
validations.name: unique-period

validations.description: Every declared indicator is present in every published quarter.
validations.name: required-values

validations.description: Every headcount is zero or greater.
validations.name: counts-are-not-negative

validations.description: The three age-band unemployment counts sum to the published total, within the rounding of one decimal place.
validations.name: age-bands-sum-to-the-total

validations.description: The male and female unemployment counts sum to the published total, within the rounding of one decimal place.
validations.name: sexes-sum-to-the-total

validations.description: Long-term unemployed people are a subset of the unemployed.
validations.name: long-term-unemployment-does-not-exceed-unemployment
